overview.headline: Free fall motion under gravity with constant acceleration

keyPoints.point: An object in free fall has only one external force from gravity expressed as weight
keyPoints.quote: An object that falls through a vacuum is subjected to only one external force, the gravitational force, expressed as the weight of the object.

keyPoints.point: Free fall acceleration stays constant and equals gravitational acceleration at sea level on Earth
keyPoints.quote: The acceleration is constant and equal to the gravitational acceleration g which is 9.8 meters per square second at sea level on the Earth.

keyPoints.point: Velocity grows linearly with time while location grows quadratically under constant acceleration
keyPoints.quote: Notice that the acceleration is a constant, the velocity increases linearly, and the location increases quadratically.

keyPoints.point: Galileo showed the relationship stayed same regardless of mass of ball used in experiment
keyPoints.quote: The relationship was the same regardless of the mass of the ball used in the experiment.

keyTerms.gloss: moving only under gravity action with no other force
keyTerms.quote: An object that is moving only because of the action of gravity is said to be free falling

keyTerms.gloss: constant acceleration from gravity near sea level on Earth
keyTerms.quote: The acceleration is constant and equal to the gravitational acceleration g which is 9.8 meters per square second at sea level on the Earth.

keyTerms.gloss: velocity gained over time under constant acceleration
keyTerms.quote: Knowing the acceleration, we can determine the velocity and location of any free falling object at any time using the following equations.

keyTerms.gloss: displacement from initial location growing with square of time
keyTerms.quote: where a is the acceleration, V is the velocity, and X is the displacement from an initial location.

keyTerms.gloss: additional force acting in atmosphere that makes motion complex
keyTerms.quote: there is an additional drag force acting on the object

keyTerms.gloss: different falling speeds limited by air resistance
keyTerms.quote: Falling cannon balls are not actually free falling – they are subject to air resistance and would fall at different terminal velocities.
